clue.text: Stage movement

definitions.meaning: a single phase or level in a process, as in 'one more stage to go'
a pace or dance move made with the feet

explanation.surface: A piece of choreography or blocking performed on a theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday synonyms: a phase in a process, and one pace of a dancer's feet.

clue.text: Appropriate line in revolutionary plan

indicators.note: in says the letter for line goes inside the turned-round plan
revolutionary means turned round, so the word for plan is read backwards

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area

explanation.surface: A rebel's scheme contains a line worth borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns MAP into PAM, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To palm something is to pocket it by sleight of hand, so it is a verb synonym for taking for oneself.

clue.text: Go before City editor blocks advance payment

indicators.note: blocks means sits in the way inside, so the City and editor letters go within the advance payment

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance, as in poker
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A City newspaper editor holds up an advance before it can go out.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede is to precede in time or order, a formal synonym for going earlier.

clue.text: Classical architect receives Dutch plant

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the letter for Dutch goes inside the architect's name

parts.note: Inigo Jones, the English architect who introduced classical Palladian style

explanation.surface: A neoclassical architect is given a plant from Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones (1573-1652) designed the Banqueting House in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigofera, the source of the blue dye, is a shrub, so the word names a plant as well as a colour.

clue.text: Shoot capturing soldiers parking tank?

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the soldiers and parking letters go within the shoot

parts.note: a scion is a young shoot or twig of a plant
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone gunning for troops at a car park, who might be a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the Scorpion was a British light tank.
explanation.definitionFit: The FV101 Scorpion is a British armoured reconnaissance vehicle, an example of an armoured fighting vehicle.

clue.text: Type of set form of matter

definitions.meaning: a kind of flat-screen television set
the ionised state of matter beyond gas, or the fluid part of blood

explanation.surface: A physics lesson about how a television set is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasma screen is a TV technology, and in physics an ionised gas counts as a fourth state alongside solid, liquid and gas.

clue.text: Feud in Mediterranean capital has purpose for everyone

indicators.note: purpose for everyone means a word for purpose stands in place of a word for everyone

parts.note: Valletta is the capital of Malta
all means everyone
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A quarrel in a Maltese city where people share a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals swapping one piece for another inside the capital of Malta.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged blood feud, originally between families in Corsica and Italy.

clue.text: This may be sung in Latin during elaborate service

indicators.note: Latin during the service means its letter falls in the middle of the rearranged word
elaborate means worked up into something new, so the letters of service are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Latin chant performed in the middle of an ornate church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' rearranges SERVICE to VERSICE, and 'during' sets L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A versicle is a short sentence sung or said by the priest in a liturgy, answered by the congregation.

clue.text: Aiming to have member accepted by Old King's school

parts.note: training a gun on something is aiming it

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the member goes inside the king's name

parts.note: Old King Cole, the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme
a leg is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: Someone looking to get a member into the old king's school.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the nursery-rhyme monarch who called for his pipe and bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A training college is an institution that prepares students for a profession, such as teaching, so it is a kind of school.

clue.text: Pageantry with European team in Italian city

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
a football or cricket team has eleven players, and 11 is drawn here as II

explanation.surface: A grand ceremony with a European side in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: A team is usually XI in crosswords; here the figures 11 are read as the letters II.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town near Naples buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Fat to be seared in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cut of fatty meat that needs searing in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obese is very overweight, so the adjective is a stronger synonym for fat.

clue.text: Stops trips around El Salvador

indicators.note: trips around El Salvador means the trips word wraps round the country code

parts.note: rides are journeys or trips
ES is the international code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: A traveller halts journeys through a Central American country.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use to stop somewhere means to stay or lodge there, a synonym for dwelling.

clue.text: Spanish manager has Italian beer and sausage

parts.note: Pep Guardiola, the Spanish football manager
Peroni is an Italian lager brand

explanation.surface: A football boss enjoying a lager and a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy cured salami, a type of sausage common as a pizza topping.

clue.text: Greek tenor seen in part of Cincinnati club

indicators.note: seen in means the tenor letter sits inside the hidden run

parts.note: a run of four letters straddling the join of these two words, the end of the city and the start of club

explanation.surface: A Greek singer performing at a Cincinnati nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ATIC sits across 'cincinnATI Club', and 'seen in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means of Attica or Athens, so it is a regional word for Greek, as in the Attic dialect.

clue.text: Ask for a bit of blue cheese soufflé

indicators.note: a bit of here takes just the opening letter of blue
a soufflé is whipped up, so the letters of cheese are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner requests a little blue cheese soufflé.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg or implore, a stronger synonym for requesting.

clue.text: Before rugby training side is deficient

indicators.note: before says the side word comes ahead of the rugby and training letters

parts.note: a bank is the side of a river
RU is short for Rugby Union
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A rugby side found wanting even before practice starts.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the British school name for gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankrupt in its extended sense means wholly lacking, as in 'bankrupt of ideas'.

clue.text: Greeting in Cornwall leads to new confrontation

indicators.note: leads to says the new letter follows on after
greeting in Cornwall means the greeting goes inside the region's letters

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, SW
how do is a casual northern English hello

explanation.surface: A friendly hello in Cornwall that turns into a stand-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How do' is an informal British greeting, short for 'how do you do'.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a final decisive clash, a synonym for a confrontation.

clue.text: Semi-existence leads to period of decay

parts.note: semi means half
life is existence

explanation.surface: A half-lived life ends in rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' links the built word to the definition; read as a whole, 'Semi-existence' also works as a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a half-life is the time taken for half of a radioactive substance to decay.

clue.text: Deny wife is held in old prison

indicators.note: wife is held in means the wife letter goes inside the deny word

parts.note: to negate is to deny or nullify

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit their wife is locked up in an ancient jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was London's notorious prison, demolished in 1904.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate Prison stood in the City of London for centuries, so it is a historic jail.

clue.text: North-African chart put up in military quarters

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: a Moor is a North African of Berber or Arab descent
to draw is to chart or plot

explanation.surface: A North African's map is pinned up in an army mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns MOORDRAW round to give WARDROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The wardroom is the officers' mess on a warship, so it is a set of service quarters.

clue.text: Fashion queen's beauty product

parts.note: ton is high fashion, as in bon ton
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A stylish monarch's skin cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A toner is a cosmetic lotion applied to tighten the skin, part of a skincare routine.

clue.text: Complete absence of sanctions in retreats

parts.note: no means none at all
OKs are approvals, sanctions in the sense of permissions

explanation.surface: Hideaways where no penalties apply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sanctions' here means approves, not punishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are secluded corners, places to retreat to, used as a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Tracks wind left to right over sierra

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above, so the sierra letter comes after
left to right says the letter for left becomes the letter for right

parts.note: to spool is to wind thread onto a reel
S is sierra in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A hunter's trail winding from west to east over mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left to right' swaps the L of SPOOL for an R.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail or footprints of an animal, so the plural means tracks.

clue.text: Rake's letter about debauched tribe

indicators.note: about means around, so the letter word wraps round the rearranged tribe

parts.note: drop someone a line means send them a short letter

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted, so the letters of tribe are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rake's note concerning a dissolute group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool but means a dissolute man; 'debauched' rearranges and 'about' wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, a synonym for a man of loose morals.

clue.text: King leaves woven baskets for animals

indicators.note: woven suggests strands interlaced, so the remaining letters of baskets are rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch abandons wicker baskets made for pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes K out of BASKETS; 'woven' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts is a general word for animals, especially large four-legged ones.

clue.text: Winger in communist vote

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A wing player taking part in a communist ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer or politician but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A redpoll is a small finch, and crosswords often call birds winged creatures or winger.

clue.text: Start off musical opening for John Lennon?

indicators.note: start off means the first letter is dropped from the word for musical

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a port is an opening, as in porthole

explanation.surface: A musical's first night staged for John Lennon.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool John Lennon Airport bears his name, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool's airport was renamed after the Beatle in 2001, an example given as a definition.

clue.text: Has leaders of Oprah Winfrey Network sacked

indicators.note: leaders of takes the first letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: Bosses of a TV network get fired.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, a synonym for having.

clue.text: Two eyes oddly required to see plays

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these words

explanation.surface: Both eyes are needed to watch theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play or trifle with it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Wrote of poetry and briefly about legal document

indicators.note: about signals moving the letters around into a new order
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of and is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone wrote verse and, in brief, discussed a legal paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts AND to AN, and 'about' rearranges WROTEOFPOETRY plus AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A power of attorney is a written instrument authorising someone to act for another in law.
